::: {.fi-standfirst}
Science knows a great deal about health, and almost none of it reaches the person
making an actual decision in a form they can use. **FRESH** is an attempt at the
missing piece: take what the evidence actually supports, make it personal and
honest, and say plainly how sure anyone can be. Not disease management. Health.

Think of it as a primary care doctor and a registered dietitian who are also data
scientists: who have read everything, who work from your data, and who tell you how
confident they are. Then add the part that actually changes behavior. Your closest
advisor, the friend who knows you well enough to be honest and knows you well enough
to be kind. A lifestyle doctor who understands the body and also understands that
choices are made inside families, budgets, neighborhoods, and habits, so advice that
ignores those is not advice. Someone who understands how beliefs get formed in the
first place, and how a person moves from a pile of facts to something closer to
wisdom. Someone who can hold every piece of available evidence up to a quality
filter before handing you any of it.

That person does not exist. It has to be accurate, actionable, accessible, and fun
all at once, and no career produces all of that and no fifteen-minute appointment
could deliver it. Meanwhile belief gets built somewhere else: at dinner, in the
answer you give a child who asks why one cereal is better than another, in the
headline you half-read. Nobody stands outside that, and nobody has ever been paid to
fix it. So I started building it. The longer version is on
[what we're doing](about.qmd).
:::
